commit.message:
feat(init): preserve unknown tags on republish; --clean drops them

Phase 1 (e0f0864) added RepoRef::extra_tags and made try_from/to_event
round-trip unknown tags at the library level. Phase 2 wires the CLI:

- new `--clean` flag on `ngit init` suppresses the pass-through and
  is treated as a substantive flag (so `ngit init --clean` against
  MyAnnouncement republishes without needing --force)
- resolve_fields cascades extra_tags from `latest_event_repo_ref(rr)`
  — same source as name/description/web/hashtags — so a co-maintainer's
  newer publish propagates new tags into the publisher's republish.
  Falls back to my own event for symmetry in MyAnnouncement
- yellow warning on stderr lists the unknown tag names when carrying
  them through, with a hint to use --clean
- publish_and_finalize plumbs fields.extra_tags into the new RepoRef
  (replacing the Phase-1 `vec![]` placeholder)

Pinned by tests/init_preserves_unknown_tags.rs (fbee463): 7 #[rstest]
cases across two OnceCell snapshots covering single-value, multi-value,
and repeated-name unknown tags under `--force` and `--force --clean`.
Also verifies repeated *known*-name tags collapse to one on republish
(the typed field is the single source of truth).

AGENTS.md gains an "Important Invariants" entry covering the parse/
emit/cascade contract so future typed-tag additions remember to update
`is_known_tag_name` and (if applicable) cascade from latest_event.

Out of scope: CoMaintainer (State D) inheritance from another
maintainer's unknown tags exercises the same cascade but isn't pinned
by an integration test in this change. The library-level round-trip
unit tests and the resolve_fields cascade are sufficient for now;
a State D test can be added if the cascade ever regresses.

commit.message:
feat(repo_ref): preserve unknown tags on try_from/to_event round-trip

RepoRef::try_from parsed only ngit's known tag names; everything else
fell through the trailing `_ => {}`. RepoRef::to_event rebuilt the
tag list from typed struct fields. Net effect: any tag a future ngit
version or third-party tool adds to a kind-30617 was silently stripped
the next time the maintainer ran `ngit init`.

Phase 1 of the round-trip pass-through:

- new field `RepoRef::extra_tags: Vec<Tag>` for tags whose first slot
  is not a name this ngit knows about
- new helper `is_known_tag_name` as the single source of truth for
  the allowlist (d, name, description, clone, web, r, relays, t,
  blossoms, maintainers, alt)
- try_from routes the catch-all: known-name extras are dropped (typed
  field is canonical, prevents duplicate emission), unknown extras
  land in `extra_tags`
- to_event appends `self.extra_tags` after blossoms so they survive
  the round-trip verbatim
- all explicit RepoRef construction sites initialise `extra_tags: vec![]`

Library-level invariants pinned by 4 new unit tests in
`repo_ref::tests::extra_tags_round_trip`:

- single-value unknown tag round-trips
- multi-value unknown tag round-trips as one tag with both values
- repeated unknown tag names survive as separate tags
- duplicate *known*-name tags don't smuggle past try_from into
  re-emission
- allowlist-vs-emitter drift catcher: parsing the canonical fixture
  must yield an empty `extra_tags`

CLI behaviour (`--clean`, yellow warning, inheritance from latest
maintainer event) is Phase 2 of this change. tests/init_preserves_
unknown_tags.rs (pinned in fbee463) still fails until Phase 2 lands;
that's the TDD hand-off contract.

commit.message:
test(init): assert unknown tags round-trip on republish

`RepoRef::try_from` parses only ngit's known tag names and
`RepoRef::to_event` rebuilds the tag list from the typed struct
fields. Anything else on the source event is silently dropped on
every republish — if a future ngit version or a third-party tool
adds a new tag, today's `ngit init` erases it the next time the
maintainer runs it.

Pin the round-trip contract before implementing it:

- preserve unknown tags by default on `ngit init --force`
- single-value, multi-value, and repeated-name shapes all survive
- repeated *known*-name tags collapse to one (typed field is the
  single source of truth)
- `--clean` strips unknown tags

Two `OnceCell`-shared snapshots, seven `#[rstest]` cases.

The new harness method
`arrange_init_state_c_my_announcement_with_extra_tags` appends
arbitrary extras to the fabricated kind-30617 before signing; the
existing zero-arg method delegates with `vec![]`.

Tests will fail until `RepoRef::extra_tags` and `ngit init --clean`
land — TDD hand-off.

commit.message:
test(git_push_pr): assert 2nd revision root anchors on original patch

Extends the force-push snapshot with a second amend + force push so the
test now exercises two consecutive revisions of the same patch series.

Confirms empirically that the second revision root's `e ... reply` tag
points at the original proposal root, not the first revision root. This
falls out of `get_all_proposals` (lib/utils.rs:208) filtering events
where `event_is_revision_root` is true, so the only candidate
`find_proposal_and_patches_by_branch_name` can return is the original
proposal — that event flows down to `generate_patch_event` as
`root_proposal_id` (git_events.rs:252) on every force push.

Two new assertions:
- revision_2_root_replies_to_original_root
- revision_2_tip_root_is_revision_2_root

Renamed six_patch_events_total -> nine_patch_events_total (count is now
2 original + 1 FF push + 3 revision #1 + 3 revision #2).

test(git_push_pr): patch->PR upgrade on plain FF push of >64KiB commit

Simpler companion to patch_update_force_to_pr: no amend, no -f. A
plain fast-forward push of a single oversized commit on top of an
existing patch series fires the size-triggered upgrade arm in

commit.message:
test(git_push_pr): assert proposal branch shorthand on fresh clone

Adds a fresh-clone (CloneLogin::None) ls-remote step at the end of
patch_update_force_to_pr to confirm the upgraded patch->PR proposal is
advertised with the original patch root id's 8-char shorthand and
resolves to the latest follow-up tip OID -- not the PR upgrade event id.

list.rs advertises proposals in two namespaces by design:
- refs/pr/<branch>(<shorthand>) and refs/pr/<event-id>/head -- every
  proposal (get_all_proposals_state, list.rs:300-334), no
  does_commit_exist filter
- refs/heads/pr/<branch>(<shorthand>) -- the user-facing remote-branch
  surface, only for open/draft proposals whose tip is locally available
  (get_open_and_draft_proposals_state, list.rs:143-296)

The assertions match refs ending in pr/<branch>(<8-hex>) without pinning
to either prefix, so the test stays correct whichever namespace the
proposal lands in.

Three new cases:
  fresh_clone_exactly_one_pr_branch
  fresh_clone_pr_branch_uses_original_root_shorthand_and_latest_tip
  fresh_clone_does_not_advertise_pr_event_shorthand_branch

The last is the load-bearing negative: revision-root filtering in
utils.rs:144-149 must mask the PR upgrade event from acting as an
independent proposal root.  If it stopped, a stray
pr/<branch>(<pr_event_8>) advertisement would appear -- which this
assertion fails on loudly.

All 19 cases (16 existing + 3 new) pass on current main.

commit.message:
test(git_push_pr): PR-update threading after patch->PR upgrade

Extends patch_update_force_to_pr with a follow-up commit + push after the
size-triggered patch->PR upgrade.  The upgraded thread root is PR-kind,
so the push must produce one KIND_PULL_REQUEST_UPDATE event whose E tag
references the upgrade PR event id -- not the original patch root.  This
is the load-bearing observable for the e66a47a fix
(effective_root = pr_upgrade_root.unwrap_or(proposal) in
git_remote_nostr/push.rs:475-478).

Snapshot now captures both stages with no cross-test side effects:
- stage 1 (immediately after the force push): pr_update_count_after_upgrade
  -- locks in that the upgrade itself emits zero updates
- final (after the follow-up push): all event counts and the
  pr_update_event itself

The existing zero_pr_update_events test is renamed to
zero_pr_update_events_after_upgrade and now reads the stage-1 count, so
it keeps asserting the same property without conflicting with the new
positive PR-update assertions.

Eight new cases:
  pr_update_event_exists
  no_new_patch_events_from_followup
  still_only_one_pr_event_after_followup
  pr_update_event_e_tag_references_pr_event
  pr_update_event_e_tag_does_not_reference_original_patch_root
  pr_update_event_p_tag_references_pr_event_author
  pr_update_event_c_tag_is_followup_tip
  pr_update_event_authored_by_maintainer

All 16 cases (8 original + 8 new) pass on current main.

commit.message:
test(git_push_pr): patch->PR upgrade on force push with >64KiB amend

Extends the patch_update_force scenario by writing a 100 KiB file when
amending the maintainer's follow-up commit, so the resulting patch
exceeds the 64 KiB threshold enforced by are_commits_too_big_for_patches
(src/lib/git/mod.rs:448-459).  That trips the size-driven branch in
git_remote_nostr/push.rs:533-552 and routes the force push through the
patch->PR upgrade path instead of emitting a 3-patch revision.

Eight cases on a single OnceCell-backed snapshot:
  three_patch_events_total (2 original + 1 FF, no new patches)
  one_pr_event
  zero_pr_update_events
  pr_event_e_tag_references_original_root
  pr_event_p_tag_references_original_root_author
  pr_event_branch_name_matches_original_series
  pr_event_c_tag_is_amended_tip
  pr_event_authored_by_maintainer

All 8 pass on current main.  Locks in the upgrade behaviour: a single
KIND_PULL_REQUEST event (not KIND_PULL_REQUEST_UPDATE, not three new
patch events) whose e/p tags back-reference the original patch-series
root and its author.

commit.message:
test(harness): add tag_values_multiple helper for repeat-name tags

tag_values returns the slots of the first matching tag — correct for
multi-value single-instance tags like clone url1 url2 url3 — but wrong
for tags that appear repeatedly as separate single-value entries.  Patch
events emit hashtag-namespace tags as separate Tag entries:

  ["t", "root"]
  ["t", "root-revision"]

so tag_values(e, "t") returns only ["root"], missing root-revision.

tests/git_push_pr/patch_update_force.rs hit this on the revision-root
detection: the three force-push patches were emitted correctly and
landed on the GRASP relay, but the helper-based search couldn't see the
root-revision tag and reported 'no patch event carries t=root-revision'
when it actually did.

Adds tag_values_multiple as the helper for the repeat-name shape and
switches patch_update_force.rs over to it.  Existing tag_values doc
clarified to call out which shape it's for.

commit.message:
test(git_push_pr): revision-root behaviour on force push after amend

A contributor publishes a patch-kind proposal (ngit send --force-patch,
two commits, no cover letter).  The maintainer clones, adds a commit
and fast-forward pushes, then amends that commit and force-pushes.

The force push must re-publish the full 3-commit series as a revision,
producing 3 new Kind::GitPatch events:
  - patch[0] (revision root): t root, t root-revision,
      e <original_root_id> _ reply
  - patch[1]: e <patch[0].id> _ root, e <patch[0].id> _ reply
  - patch[2] (tip): e <patch[0].id> _ root, e <patch[1].id> _ reply

Eight cases on a single OnceCell-backed snapshot:
  six_patch_events_total (2 original + 1 FF + 3 revision)
  zero_pr_events
  zero_pr_update_events
  revision_root_has_t_root
  revision_root_has_t_revision_root
  revision_root_replies_to_original_root
  tip_patch_root_is_revision_root
  tip_patch_replies_to_second_patch

All 8 cases currently FAIL — regression introduced by e66a47a.

commit.message:
test(git_push_pr): patch-kind stays patch-kind on follow-up push

Regression coverage for push.rs:655-658.  A fresh contributor
publishes a patch-series proposal via `ngit send --force-patch`;
the maintainer clones, checks out the advertised remote-tracking
`pr/<branch>(<shorthand>)` branch, commits, and `git push`es.

The push must produce another Kind::GitPatch event, never a
KIND_PULL_REQUEST and never a KIND_PULL_REQUEST_UPDATE — the latter
two kinds are only legal when the root proposal is itself PR-kind.

Five cases on a single shared snapshot:
- three_patch_events_total (2 originals + 1 push update)
- zero_pr_events
- zero_pr_update_events
- update_patch_authored_by_maintainer
- update_patch_commit_tag_is_new_tip

Uses the maintainer's identity for the follow-up push as a
convenience; the contributor's nsec is not exposed by
Harness::publish_patch_series and push.rs:481-484 already accepts
repo maintainers in addition to the proposal author.

commit.message:
fix: prevent PR downgrade and correctly root PR updates after upgrade

send.rs -- downgrade protection:
- extract existing_thread_is_pr as a named bool separate from the
  broader should_be_pr
- bail when --force-patch is used on an existing PR thread; the error
  message directs the user to --force-pr for a PR update instead
- update --force-patch doc string to mention the restriction

utils.rs -- pr_upgrade_root helper:
- add pr_upgrade_root(commits_events) which finds the KIND_PULL_REQUEST
  event (if any) that was emitted when a patch was upgraded to a PR
- thread it as the third element of the (proposal, chain, pr_upgrade_root)
  tuple returned by get_all_proposals / get_open_or_draft_proposals and
  find_proposal_and_patches_by_branch_name

git_remote_nostr/push.rs -- correct effective_root for all push paths:
- compute effective_root = pr_upgrade_root.unwrap_or(proposal)
  once per proposal; this is the event passed as root_proposal to
  generate_patches_or_pr_event_or_pr_updates
- for normal PRs (proposal is KIND_PULL_REQUEST), pr_upgrade_root is
  None so effective_root == proposal -- no behaviour change
- for upgraded patches, effective_root is the PR kind event so all
  subsequent PR updates correctly E-tag the PR root, never a PR update,
  regardless of how many PR updates have already occurred
- for plain patch threads, effective_root is the original patch so new
  revisions continue to e-tag the original (not a prior revision)
- replace the old tip_is_pr_or_update / patches.first() heuristic which
  incorrectly overwrote effective_root for normal PRs with existing updates

commit.message:
fix: compute PR merge-base from git topology, not stored event tag

Previously the merge-base for PR events generated by git push was
computed using a mix of strategies:
- new PR / force push: get_commit_parent(first_commit) — only correct
  when ahead is computed relative to origin/main
- FF push on existing PR (840c581): read the merge-base tag from the
  root PR event — correct for FF, but wrong after a rebase (stale tag)

This introduced a special is_force_push flag to distinguish the two
cases, but the underlying issue is that the merge-base was derived from
stored nostr state rather than from the git DAG.

Fix: add get_merge_base(a, b) to RepoActions (thin wrapper around
libgit2's merge_base()), and use it unconditionally inside
generate_patches_or_pr_event_or_pr_updates to compute the fork point
as git merge-base(tip, origin/main). This is correct for all three
push types and removes all reliance on stored event tag values:
- new PR: merge-base(tip, main) = fork point ✓
- FF push: merge-base(tip, main) = original fork point ✓
- force push after rebase: merge-base(tip, main) = new fork point ✓

Drop is_force_push parameter and the pr_merge_base / str_to_sha1 /
tag_value machinery that was reading from the event tag.

commit.message:
test: git_push_pr::new_pr — grasp-default PR kind regression suite

Ten rstest cases covering the 9e06e7b 'default to PR kind when repo has
a GRASP server' change, exercised via git push -u origin pr/feature:

- pr_event_exactly_one: single KIND_PULL_REQUEST on the GRASP (9e06e7b fired)
- zero_patch_events: no Kind::GitPatch emitted (overlap regression)
- zero_pr_update_events: no KIND_PULL_REQUEST_UPDATE on a first-time push
- contributor_pr_remote_tracking_matches_local: refs/remotes/origin/pr/feature
  = local tip (covers update_remote_refs_pushed at push.rs:165-170)
- upstream_tracking_config_set: branch.pr/feature.merge set by -u flag
- grasp_has_refs_nostr_for_pr: refs/nostr/<event_id> in bare repo = tip
- pr_event_branch_name_tag_is_feature: pr/ prefix stripped correctly
- pr_event_c_tag_is_tip: c tag = pushed tip OID
- pr_event_a_tag_is_repo_coordinate: a tag encodes 30617:<pubkey>:<id>
- new_clone_lists_pr_feature_branch: ls-remote shows pr/feature(<8-hex>)

Layout mirrors tests/git_push_state/: directory under tests/git_push_pr/
with main.rs declaring the new_pr submodule, plus Cargo.toml [[test]] entry.

test: git_push_pr::new_pr — grasp-default PR kind regression suite

Ten rstest cases covering the 9e06e7b 'default to PR kind when repo has
a GRASP server' change, exercised via git push -u origin pr/feature:

- pr_event_exactly_one: single KIND_PULL_REQUEST on the GRASP (9e06e7b fired)
- zero_patch_events: no Kind::GitPatch emitted (overlap regression)
- zero_pr_update_events: no KIND_PULL_REQUEST_UPDATE on a first-time push
- contributor_pr_remote_tracking_matches_local: refs/remotes/origin/pr/feature
  = local tip (covers update_remote_refs_pushed at push.rs:165-170)
- upstream_tracking_config_set: branch.pr/feature.merge set by -u flag
- grasp_has_refs_nostr_for_pr: refs/nostr/<event_id> in bare repo = tip
- pr_event_branch_name_tag_is_feature: pr/ prefix stripped correctly
- pr_event_c_tag_is_tip: c tag = pushed tip OID
- pr_event_a_tag_is_repo_coordinate: a tag encodes 30617:<pubkey>:<id>
- new_clone_lists_pr_feature_branch: ls-remote shows pr/feature(<8-hex>)

Layout mirrors tests/git_push_state/: directory under tests/git_push_pr/
with main.rs declaring the new_pr submodule, plus Cargo.toml [[test]] entry.

  from all seven test files; import from test_harness instead
- Drop 'use std::path::Path' from all seven test files (no longer needed)

commit.message:
refactor: lift duplicated test plumbing into test_harness

Pass 1 (nostr constants + event helpers):
- Add test_harness::nostr with KIND_PULL_REQUEST (1618),
  KIND_PULL_REQUEST_UPDATE (1619), KIND_REPO_STATE (30618),
  tag_value, tag_values, and event_branch_name_tag.
- Re-export all six from test_harness::lib so tests use
  'use test_harness::KIND_PULL_REQUEST' etc.
- scenarios.rs drops its private KIND_PULL_REQUEST, STATE_KIND,
  and event_branch_name_tag copies and imports from the new module.

Pass 2 (GraspServer + Repo ergonomics):
- GraspServer::read_nostr_ref(npub, identifier, event_id_hex)
  folds the git_data_path/<npub>/<id>.git + git-for-each-ref lookup
  that send_pr.rs/send_pr_update.rs/send_pr_update_rebase.rs all
  reimplement inline (~20 lines each).
- Repo::git_ok(args, label) runs git and bails on non-zero with
  captured stdout/stderr — replaces the local run_git/run_git_ok
  helpers duplicated across five test files.
- Repo::rev_parse(rev) wraps git rev-parse + UTF-8 parse —
  replaces the git_rev_parse helper duplicated in three test files.

No existing test files are modified; the existing send_pr* helpers
remain in place and will be removed in a follow-up migration.
